method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula comparison and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All five translated content blocks in the rationals section, including the quotient construction, operation/order definitions, correction note and exercises.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A rational i/j uses integer numerator and nonzero integer denominator and can be encoded by a pair, but pairs cannot be rationals directly because 3/2 and 6/4 are equal while their pairs differ. Ratequiv identifies pairs exactly by cross multiplication.
samples.checks: The domain excludes zero denominators, both motivating equalities remain, the cross-product iff is exact, and the equivalence-relation exercise precedes the quotient definition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Rationals are Ratequiv equivalence classes of integer pairs whose second component is nonzero.
samples.checks: The full quotient expression Rat=(Int×(Int\{0_Int}))/Ratequiv is structurally unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Addition and multiplication of rational classes use the displayed common-denominator and componentwise-product representatives. Order is defined by requiring s−r to have a nonnegative numerator and positive denominator.
samples.checks: Every representative formula is unchanged. The isolated English r−s typo was corrected to s−r because the preceding clause and following display both require s−r; MRARITH-001 records the delta.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Well-definedness is deferred to the checking section. Each integer i is embedded as the rational class [i,1], and the exercise asks that this embedding preserve addition, multiplication and order.
samples.checks: Both references, the embedding formula and all three compatibility formulas are preserved.
